plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers that brighten the late winter landscape. Hundreds of cultivars exist, with single, semi-double, and fully double forms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (December to April in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is closely related to Camellia sinensis, the plant used to make tea, and its seed oil has long been used in Japan for hair care and cooking.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that flowers on bare branches before its leaves emerge. Its fragrant blossoms often open in cold weather, sometimes while snow is still on the ground.
plants.location: Native to southern China; cultivated across East Asia, especially in China, Japan, and Korea
plants.funFact: In Chinese culture the plum blossom is one of the 'Three Friends of Winter' and symbolizes perseverance and hope because it blooms in the harshest season.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with drooping, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It carpets woodlands and gardens, often pushing up through frost and snow.
plants.location: Native to Europe from the Pyrenees to Ukraine; naturalized in the United Kingdom and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops produce galantamine, a compound that has been developed into a medication used to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking shrub with the largest flower head in the protea family, made of pointed pink bracts surrounding a central cluster of tiny flowers. It thrives in fynbos on nutrient-poor soils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer, with peak blooms from late summer to early autumn, though flowering may occur in some months of the year
plants.location: South Africa's Western and Eastern Cape fynbos; cultivated in Australia, Hawaii, and California
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, and its thick underground stems help it survive and resprout after the wildfires that regularly sweep through its habitat.
